name: Guyana
headline: Guyana began a national electronic health record in 2026, but its 2023 data protection law still has no commencement order.

access.summary: The Data Protection Act 2023 promises a free copy within one month, but no commencement order had been shown by September 2026. The 2011 Access to Information Act reaches public hospital files, slowly, so this sits near the top of the no-enforceable-right band.
detail: Section 11 of the Data Protection Act 2023 gives a right to a copy of one's personal data, in electronic form if asked electronically. Controllers must act within one month, extendable by two months, and the first copy is free.

The Act starts only on a day the Minister appoints by order. Demerara Waves reported on 31 March 2026 that no order had been issued, and on 30 September 2026 the 592 Guardian said commencement has never been shown.

The Access to Information Act 2011 gives every citizen a right to official documents of public authorities, including Regional Health Authorities and state bodies. Requests go through the Commissioner of Information, with up to 60 days to decide.

Officials said at the January 2026 EHR launch that patients would see their records on their phones. The app's verified use is booking: about 500 online appointments by March 2026. Record viewing by patients was not verified.

control.summary: The new EHR follows a "one patient, one record" rule across public facilities, with no opt-out and no access log a patient can see. Access is role-based and staff entries are traceable, but the consent rules of the 2023 Act are not in force.
detail: GPHC describes the EHR as "one patient, one record": wherever a patient seeks care in the public system, their history follows them. No route to opt out of this sharing was found.
The polyclinic's acting head told DPI in March 2026 that access is role-based. DPI added that individual logins make all entries traceable. No way for a patient to see that log was found.
The 2023 Act lists a health record as sensitive personal data, but allows processing for medical purposes by a health professional without consent. It is not yet in force.

privacy.summary: With the 2023 Act not commenced, no data protection office enforces anything yet, so this sits below the general-law band. A Commissioner was appointed in 2026 but also runs the digital ID registry, and no health data breach was found.
detail: No health-sector enforcement was found and the general law is not in force, so this is scored below the 45 to 66 band for general law, as for Belize.

Once in force, the Act would require breach notice to the Commissioner within 72 hours where feasible. Breaching the data protection principles, including security, carries fines up to GY$100 million or five years in prison on indictment.

Aneal Giddings was appointed Data Protection Commissioner in early 2026. In May he wrote that his office was still being formally established and that the Act was not yet fully operational. He also administers the digital ID registry.
The health minister said in December 2025 that patient data is protected by Ministry protocols written with Mount Sinai, while conceding the Act's commencement order had not been issued.

commercial.summary: No law in force limits the sale or marketing use of health data. The 2023 Act would make health records sensitive data, give a right to stop direct marketing and punish selling unlawfully obtained data, but it has not started.
detail: The 2023 Act lists a health record as sensitive personal data. Section 17 would let a person object to direct marketing, including profiling, after which the data may no longer be used for it.
Selling personal data obtained without the controller's consent would be an offence, with fines up to GY$500 million or ten years in prison on indictment.
None of this applies until the Act is commenced. No rules on health apps, data brokers or sales of de-identified data were found.

journey.summary: A national EHR built by RioMed went live at one Georgetown polyclinic in January 2026 and was being phased into Georgetown Public Hospital from June. Lab reports, diagnostic results and prescriptions are linked at those sites, but most facilities were not yet connected.
detail: The Ministry launched the National Electronic Health Record at Festival City Polyclinic on 17 January 2026, under a US$3.3 million contract with UK firm RioMed. Plans run to GPHC, then all public facilities, then the private sector.

At the polyclinic, registration, consultation and pharmacy are fully digital. GPHC says diagnostic results, lab reports and prescriptions are accessible across specialties, with prescriptions going straight to pharmacies.
In June 2026 the minister said GPHC rollout was phased, starting with urgent care. President Ali said in February that over 100,000 children have baseline screening data in the digital system.
No national claims system was found to link. Guyana is outside the EU, so the European Health Data Space does not apply.

clinical.summary: Clinicians at Festival City Polyclinic, about 128 assessments a day, and in GPHC departments as they come online see one unified record. Elsewhere in the public system and in private practice, records are still paper or separate.
detail: DPI reported in March 2026 that a patient seen in chronic disease, surgery or cardiology clinics now has one record, with about 128 clinical assessments a day logged at the polyclinic.
GPHC began deploying the EHR in phases from June 2026, starting with urgent care before surgical, medical and outpatient departments.
Records from other public facilities and private providers are not yet in the system. No emergency access or consent rules for clinicians were found.

research.summary: No consent rule or opt-out governs research use of health data, since the 2023 Act is not in force. One safeguard counts: the Ministry of Health's Institutional Review and Ethics Board reviews research involving human participants, material and data.
detail: Once in force, section 36 of the 2023 Act would treat research use as compatible with the original purpose and exempt it from the access right if results do not identify anyone.
Section 17 would let a person object to research use on grounds of their situation, unless the work is a public-interest task. Neither provision operates yet.
The Ministry's IRB reviews research proposals and aims to protect participants in health research, including human material and data. No public register of data uses was found.

ai.summary: No law, guidance or device rule for clinical AI was found, yet public hospitals already use AI. Enmore hospital pilots AI reading of X-rays, and about 300 physicians are to test the OpenEvidence tool.
detail: The health minister said in January 2026 that Enmore Regional Hospital pilots AI reading of digital X-rays, which he put at close to 99% accuracy. No independent evaluation was found.
In September 2026 he said about 300 physicians and some nurses would get OpenEvidence, an AI tool that summarises medical literature to support treatment decisions.
The Ministry and Mount Sinai held a seminar on integrating AI into care in April 2026. No regulator or approval route for AI software as a medical device was found.

journeyNote: One EHR links registration, labs, diagnostics and pharmacy at Festival City Polyclinic and parts of GPHC. School screening data is digital. Other public facilities, private care and any claims link were not connected or not verified.

laws.name: Data Protection Act 2023 (Act No. 18 of 2023)
laws.what: Health records are sensitive data; free copy within one month, 72-hour breach notice. No commencement order shown.

laws.name: Access to Information Act 2011 (Act No. 21 of 2011)
laws.what: Right to official documents of public authorities, including Regional Health Authorities, via the Commissioner of Information.

laws.name: Digital Identity Card Act 2023 (Act No. 19 of 2023)
laws.what: National digital ID, in force since 31 March 2026; registry run by the Data Protection Commissioner.

news.headline: Online paper asks government whether the Data Protection Act was ever commenced
news.why: Without the Act in force, patients have no enforceable right to their record or a working regulator.

news.headline: About 300 doctors to test OpenEvidence AI tool, health minister says
news.why: AI enters treatment decisions with no clinical-AI rules in place.

news.headline: Electronic health record rollout begins at Georgetown Public Hospital
news.why: The main referral hospital joining the record is the biggest step toward one connected record.

news.headline: Data Protection Commissioner says his office is still being set up
news.why: Patients have nowhere yet to complain if their health data is misused.

news.headline: National electronic health record goes live at Georgetown polyclinic
news.why: Starts the move from paper to one record per patient across public care.
